summary: AWS <> GCP authorization path mismatch preventing cross-account service role assumption in staging
description: Issue summary: On-call engineers are unable to assume the cross-account AWS role that our staging runner uses when accessing S3 and secrets for canary inference runs. Investigation shows the problem originates from a mismatch between the AWS IAM role trust policy and the GCP workload identity binding created by the terraform module. This ticket tracks diagnosis and remediation.
impact: On-call and SREs cannot run staging canaries that exercise end-to-end inference path. This blocks some CI workflows and makes it harder to validate rollouts before production. No production user-facing impact observed yet, but risk of delayed rollout validation for Dedicated features.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Login to staging bastion (us-east) as ops user
2) Trigger canary pipeline job redwood-canary/staging via CI (uses gcp-k8s service account -> AWS role assume flow)
3) Observe assume-role failure in CI logs: 'AccessDenied: Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRole'

4) Run gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy for k8s GSA; run aws sts assume-role with the same external-id and role arn — fails from non-privileged runner but succeeds from a developer laptop with different identity mapping
observed_behavior: sts:AssumeRole requests from the GKE node pool service identity are denied. Cloud Audit logs show workload identity token was exchanged, but the AWS role's trust policy condition on 'sts:ExternalId' does not match the value embedded in the token exchange manifest generated by the terraform module.
expected_behavior: Staging workload identity mapping should allow the GKE service account (via GSA) to assume the correct AWS role using the external-ids produced by our provisioning pipeline. Canary jobs should complete without manual token workarounds.
logs: ci: pipeline redwood-canary/staging - job 37 failed with exit code 1 - see log snippet: 'AccessDenied: Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRole'
investigation_notes: Checked terraform state for module 'crosscloud/role-bindings' - the aws_iam_role resource trust policy contains an ExternalId of 'wrld-ops-staging-v2' but terraform plan shows no pending changes (possible drift introduced by earlier manual amend).

GCP workload identity binding in GCP console shows principal: 'serviceAccount:redwood-staging-canary-gsa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com' bound to AWS role via OIDC, but the terraform template in infra repo used old external-id template variable (wrld-ops-staging).

Cross-checked CloudTrail for successful assume requests from dev laptops: those used a different external id string 'dev-ops-local' and succeed because their assumed role mapping uses a separate trust alias. This explains why only CI/GKE fails.

Pulled related Git commits: infra/iam: b3d4e5f updated external-id values for prod-only roles on 2026-02-18 (PR #492). Staging variables were not updated in that PR and later someone manually edited the AWS role in console on 2026-03-02 (support note 2026-03-03 Slack #infra).

Auth flows tested: swapping external-id on a staging role to match GSA token allowed assume-role in an isolated test (manual edit), confirming the root cause is mismatched external-id condition in role trust policy.
temporary_workarounds: 1) Manual edit: Update AWS role trust policy ExternalId to 'wrld-ops-staging' to match terraform output for now (done 2026-03-10 03:15 UTC) — short-term workaround applied but will be reverted when infra fix lands.
2) Run canary from a dev VM that has a different role mapping (requires manual step and is not scalable).
proposed_remediation: Synchronize terraform variables and state: update infra module to standardize external-id naming scheme (use parameterized value from terraform workspace 'staging'), run 'terraform plan/apply' in staging account to reconcile state, and add a CI check that validates aws_iam_role trust policy ExternalId matches workload-identity mapping. Also add a one-time migration runbook to revert the manual edit after apply.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary pipeline redwood-canary/staging completes successfully without manual role edits
2) No manual trust-policy edits required for 7 days post-deployment
3) Automated check in infra-ci flags mismatches on PRs
4) Confluence runbook updated with rollback steps and owner assigned
action_items: A. Infra: update infra/iam module to expose external-id variable and default to 'wrld-ops-${terraform.workspace}' (owner: @liamc) - target: 2026-03-15
B. Security: review trust-policy conditions for all staging roles and sign off (owner: @mira-patel) - target: 2026-03-16
C. SRE: run terraform apply in staging with state lock and verify canary (owner: @sre-oncall) - target: 2026-03-16
D. Developer-ops: add infra-ci check to PRs to compare generated external-id with existing role (owner: @devops-team) - target: 2026-03-20
